title: Bypass the ALU result mux for memory addresses
motivation: The measured critical path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding, EX, and the ALU before reaching the data memory address. Load and store addresses are always rs1 plus the decoded immediate, but currently share the ALU's general result selection logic with every RV32IM operation.

hypothesis.motivation: The measured critical path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding, EX, and the ALU before reaching the data memory address. hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a dedicated rs1-plus-immediate address sum in EX and select it directly into the EX/MEM result for loads and stores. This removes the general ALU operation result mux from the memory-address path while preserving the existing forwarding, address value, and pipeline timing. The extra adder is expected to be small compared with shortening the measured critical path.

title: Register older-result forwarding matches
motivation: The measured worst path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and runs through forwarding selection and EX to the data-memory address. Comparing that destination against both source registers in the EX cycle adds control delay before the ALU address calculation.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Compute the dependency match against the current EX/MEM writer while the consumer is in ID, then latch two pending MEM/WB-forward flags into ID/EX. Preserve the flags with ID/EX stalls and clear them on bubbles; ID-stage write-through and load-use interlocks retain the existing operand timing.

title: Predict backward branches in fetch
motivation: The current core resolves every conditional branch in EX and redirects even when the fetch stream is already on the correct path. Taken loop branches therefore discard younger instructions and add bubbles. CoreMark contains repeated loop branches, so predicting backward branches in fetch should reduce its control-flow penalty with little predictor state.

hypothesis.motivation: The current core resolves every conditional branch in EX and redirects even when the fetch stream is already on the correct path. Taken loop branches therefore discard younger instructions and add bubbles. hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a static backward-taken, forward-not-taken predictor in IF, with direct JAL predicted taken. Form the target from the fetched instruction, advance the PC to that target only when the instruction is accepted, and carry the predicted direction through ID/EX. EX should redirect and flush only when the resolved next PC differs from the prediction; a misprediction restores the correct target or sequential PC. This should remove the recurring taken-loop redirect bubbles while keeping the existing in-order retirement and bus-stall behavior.

title: Pipeline the divider out of the EX critical path
motivation: The measured critical path repeatedly runs through forwarding, EX, and the ALU, with roughly 198 ns arrival time. The combinational signed and unsigned divide and remainder operators sit in that ALU result cone even though CoreMark's common address and integer operations do not need them.

hypothesis.motivation: The measured critical path repeatedly runs through forwarding, EX, and the ALU, with roughly 198 ns arrival time. The combinational signed and unsigned divide and remainder operators sit in that ALU result cone even though CoreMark's common address and integer operations do not need them.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the combinational DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapaths with a shared radix-2 restoring divider that performs four quotient bits per cycle, taking eight cycles per divide. Keep its state in the EX unit and hold younger pipeline work until the result is ready, then retire exactly once with the existing RV32M divide-by-zero, overflow, signedness, and remainder semantics. Preserve the formal ALTOPS result substitutions with the same completion and retirement protocol. This removes the long divider chain from ordinary EX operations while bounding divide latency below the formal 20-step check depth; CoreMark is expected to gain Fmax with little cycle cost if it rarely divides.

title: Predict JALR returns with a return stack
motivation: The current fetch predictor handles backward conditional branches and direct JALs, but leaves JALR returns sequential. Each correctly predicted call can therefore still be followed by a return redirect that flushes younger work. CoreMark makes repeated function calls and returns, so a small return-address stack can remove recurring indirect-jump penalties while retaining the existing branch policy.

hypothesis.motivation: The current fetch predictor handles backward conditional branches and direct JALs, but leaves JALR returns sequential. Each correctly predicted call can therefore still be followed by a return redirect that flushes younger work. CoreMark makes repeated function calls and returns, so a small return-address stack can remove recurring indirect-jump penalties while retaining the existing branch policy.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a small hardware return-address stack (RAS), updated once when a jump resolves in EX. Push the sequential return PC for JAL/JALR calls that write x1 or x5, and pop on the common return form JALR through x1 or x5 with rd=x0. In IF, predict that return JALR to the RAS top when nonempty; otherwise keep the current sequential fallback. Carry the predicted next PC with the instruction and make EX redirect only when its resolved successor differs. Gate RAS updates when EX is held so bus stalls cannot repeat a push or pop. This targets the repeated JALR misprediction bubbles without changing branch direction prediction or retirement behavior.

title: Shorten the divider recurrence
motivation: The best implementation has moved its critical path into the EX divider, ending at div_result_q. Each cycle currently unrolls four restoring quotient-bit steps, putting four wide compare/subtract decisions in series. Shortening that recurrence should improve Fmax, while DIV/REM are rare in CoreMark.

hypothesis.motivation: The best implementation has moved its critical path into the EX divider, ending at div_result_q. Each cycle currently unrolls four restoring quotient-bit steps, putting four wide compare/subtract decisions in series. Shortening that recurrence should improve Fmax, while DIV/REM are rare in CoreMark.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Change the shared restoring divider to process two quotient bits per cycle instead of four. Widen the iteration counter and update its terminal count so all 32 bits are still processed over 16 chunks; preserve signed magnitude conversion, divide-by-zero and overflow behavior, result correction, and the formal ALTOPS substitution. The shorter serial compare/subtract chain should raise Fmax, with modest CoreMark cycle impact if DIV/REM instructions are infrequent.

title: Learn branch direction with a small BHT
motivation: The existing backward-taken, forward-not-taken policy removes many CoreMark loop bubbles, but it cannot learn a forward branch that is usually taken or a backward branch that is usually not taken. Those repeated branches still redirect the fetch stream after EX resolves them. A small direction table can adapt while retaining the static policy before an entry has been trained.

hypothesis.motivation: The existing backward-taken, forward-not-taken policy removes many CoreMark loop bubbles, but it cannot learn a forward branch that is usually taken or a backward branch that is usually not taken. Those repeated branches still redirect the fetch stream after EX resolves them. A small direction table can adapt while retaining the static policy before an entry has been trained.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a 16-entry, two-bit saturating branch direction table indexed by instruction PC. Keep one valid bit per entry and use the current backward-taken, forward-not-taken rule for untrained entries; trained conditional branches use their counter's high bit to choose between the already available branch target and PC+4. Update the table once a valid conditional branch reaches EX/MEM, using its resolved branch outcome, and preserve the existing redirect-on-next-PC-mismatch recovery. This can learn recurring branch behavior that disagrees with the static heuristic without adding a target lookup or changing retirement and stall handling.

title: Simplify branch redirect detection
motivation: The current worst path runs from the register file through EX and fetch/hazard control back to an ID-stage operand register. Branch resolution in EX is on that path because its result controls redirect and wrong-path flushing. The redirect decision currently selects full 32-bit successor PCs and compares them, even though a conditional branch's miss status follows directly from its taken outcome and prediction.

hypothesis.hypothesis: For conditional branches, detect a prediction miss directly from the resolved branch outcome and the carried predicted-taken bit instead of comparing two 32-bit next-PC values. Keep the existing successor comparison for jumps, including JALR, so target and misalignment behavior stay intact. This removes a wide comparator and next-PC selection from the common branch-to-fetch redirect path while preserving branch semantics, forwarding, and pipeline timing.

title: Use tagged branch histories
motivation: The static backward-taken policy handles loop branches, but forward branches that are usually taken still cause EX redirects. The previous small BHT let branches with matching low PC bits train the same counter, so its learned predictions were unreliable. Tags can reject those conflicting histories while preserving the static policy for unseen branches.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the untagged direction table experiment with a 32-entry tagged BHT in fetch. Index entries with PC[6:2], store PC[14:7] as the tag alongside a valid bit and two-bit saturating counter, and use the current backward-taken/forward-not-taken rule on a tag miss. On a hit, predict from the counter's high bit. Update once when a valid conditional branch reaches EX/MEM; replace the tag and initialize a weak counter toward the resolved outcome on a miss, or saturate the existing counter on a hit. Keep the existing EX redirect-on-next-PC-mismatch recovery. This should learn recurring forward-branch behavior without letting unrelated branches share direction history, with a modest table sized to reduce aliasing while limiting fetch-path and state cost.

title: Decouple redirect squash from ID operands

hypothesis.hypothesis: On a redirect, let the fetched instruction bits and register addresses continue into ID while marking the instruction invalid.
